data.narrative:
Vention is a Series C robotics and manufacturing automation company founded by Etienne Lacroix and Max Windisch that has raised $95M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comp universe of 9 private robotics firms at Series B–D stages (Exotec, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Hadrian, and others valued $1.0B–$2.0B) and 1 public comparable.

Two methods triangulate the valuation. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $156M raised proxy, implying $265M. Peer-median analysis across 7 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.6B, with a range of $1.0B–$2.0B. The disparity reflects the early-stage capital base relative to later-stage peer multiples and the wide variance in robotics valuations driven by technology differentiation and market-readiness assumptions.

Triangulation supports a valuation range of $225M (floor) to $1.9B (ceiling), with a median implied value of $958M. The wide range reflects material uncertainty around unit economics, commercialization trajectory, and whether Vention's technology footprint justifies late-stage peer multiples. Stage-progression suggests conservative $265M; peer medians suggest $1.0B–$1.6B depending on growth profile assumptions. Tightening this range requires clarity on revenue run rate, gross margins, and customer concentration.
